channel.title: Paksh: Health
channel.description: Paksh maps how India's media covers every story — coverage, gaps, and how it develops, in English and Hindi.

item.title: India's Polio Vaccination Efforts Emphasize Continued Surveillance
item.description: India's ongoing efforts to maintain its polio-free status require a dual approach of vaccination and continued surveillance. Public health messaging highlights the importance of ensuring children's polio vaccination schedules are up to… Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 1 · Right 0.

item.title: US Loses Measles Elimination Status After 26 Years
item.description: The United States has lost its measles elimination status, a designation it held for 26 years. Officials announced that both the U.S. and Mexico have had their measles elimination statuses revoked. A health organization was set to announce… Coverage: Left 4 · Centre 7 · Right 0.

item.title: Measles cases resurge in the United States
item.description: Measles cases have resurfaced in the United States, prompting concern and discussion about the implications of this resurgence. The situation has led to calls for action, with one opinion piece advocating for a 'zero dose' approach. Coverage: Left 2 · Centre 1 · Right 0.

item.title: Drug Mimicking Viagra Shows Promise in Slowing Alzheimer's Progression
item.description: A drug that mimics the effects of Viagra has shown promise in slowing the progression of Alzheimer's disease, offering potential hope for treatment. Alzheimer's is characterized by irreversible cognitive decline and memory loss. While… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: WHO Warns of 39 Million Deaths from Antimicrobial Resistance
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued a warning regarding the threat of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), stating it could lead to 39 million deaths over the next 25 years. The organization is sounding the alarm on this growing… Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 1 · Right 0.

item.title: Weight-loss drug study shows success in young children
item.description: A study has demonstrated the success of weight-loss drugs in children as young as six years old. The research, which involved elementary-age children, indicates a new potential frontier for these medications. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: US, Mexico, Bolivia Lose Measles-Free Status Amid Rising Deaths
item.description: The United States, Mexico, and Bolivia have lost their measles-free status due to a rise in cases and deaths. This decline is attributed to falling vaccination rates in the US. The specific number of deaths or cases was not provided in the… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: Menopause and Mental Health Evidence
item.description: Evidence suggests a link between menopause and mental health issues, with hormonal changes during this phase potentially impacting mood and cognitive function. Research indicates that understanding these connections is crucial for… Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 1 · Right 0.

item.title: India to Launch First Indigenous H5N1 Bird Flu Vaccine for Chickens
item.description: India is set to launch its first indigenously developed vaccine against the H5N1 bird flu strain for chickens on November 20. The vaccine is intended to protect poultry from the avian influenza virus. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 1 · Right 1.

item.title: Kenya's last Ebola patient discharged from hospital
item.description: Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient from the hospital, marking the beginning of a 42-day countdown to the country being declared disease-free. The patient's release signifies a critical step in controlling the recent outbreak. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: FDA Warns of Rare Blindness Risk with GLP-1 Drugs
item.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a new warning regarding GLP-1 drugs, including a potential link to a rare eye condition that can cause sudden blindness. The warning advises adding information about this risk to the… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 5 · Right 0.

item.title: FDA Warns of Potential Vision Loss Risk with Weight Loss Drugs
item.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a warning regarding a potential risk of optic nerve damage associated with GLP-1 drugs, such as semaglutide and tirzepatide, commonly used for diabetes and weight loss. Experts advise… Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 0 · Right 1.

item.title: Scientists Resolve Two-Decade Mystery Linking Gut Bacterium to Colon Cancer
item.description: Researchers at Johns Hopkins University have identified how a common gut bacterium's toxin can increase the risk of colon cancer, resolving a mystery that has persisted for about 20 years. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 0 · Right 3.

item.title: Merck/Moderna cancer vaccine shows 42% reduction in melanoma risk
item.description: A cancer vaccine developed by Merck and Moderna has demonstrated a 42% reduction in the risk of death or recurrence for patients with melanoma. Following the release of this data, Moderna's shares experienced a significant decline, falling… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: First Human Shamonda Virus Case Confirmed in France; Patient Dies
item.description: France has confirmed the first-ever human case of the Shamonda virus, a livestock virus, in a man in his 60s who later died. The patient was severely immunocompromised when he fell ill in early October. French health authorities described… Coverage: Left 3 · Centre 4 · Right 0.

item.title: Christina Applegate reveals misdiagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis
item.description: Actress Christina Applegate has stated that she was misdiagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis (MS). The news of the misdiagnosis was described as devastating. The coverage does not specify the timeline of the misdiagnosis or the subsequent… Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 7 · Right 0.

item.title: Ontario revises drug funding rules, impacting cancer patients
item.description: Ontario has revised its drug funding rules, leading to disappointment among cancer patients who previously relied on out-of-country coverage. The changes have prompted some patients to seek treatments abroad, with one report highlighting… Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV diagnosed with lung cancer, undergoes surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with adenocarcinoma, a type of lung cancer. Following the diagnosis, he underwent surgery in Rome where a portion of his lung was removed. The Vatican has issued health updates confirming the surgery was… Coverage: Left 6 · Centre 16 · Right 3.

item.title: Hepatitis B Drug Approved; Study Warns of Case Surge Under New Guidelines
item.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved a new drug for Hepatitis B that may assist patients in achieving a functional cure. Separately, a study suggests that new vaccine guidelines could lead to a surge in Hepatitis B… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 1 · Right 1.
